henderson.story:
Henderson Family Trust: what an advisory relationship could add

WHY WE ARE TALKING NOW
• NVDA is 22.9% of the account: single-company concentration warrants a discussion.
• MSFT is 10.6% of the account including funds, above the 10% guideline.
• The CIO moved technology from overweight to neutral on 20 October, citing crowded positioning and this policy risk. Research keeps a Buy on NVDA but cut its 2027 estimate 4%.

WHAT THE PROGRAM COULD DO FOR YOU
• A fiduciary relationship: we monitor and rebalance the portfolio to our CIO's allocation for your profile, which our illustrative assumptions put about +0.51 points a year ahead of today's mix before costs.
• A tax-aware plan to reduce NVDA.
• More choices: 8 strategies, including CIO models, separate account managers and direct indexing; for you, CIO Model Portfolio (ETF), Core Equity Direct Indexing, Municipal Ladder SMA.
• No commissions: trading is included (about $45K a year today).

WHAT ONLY A MANAGED ACCOUNT CAN DO
• Direct indexing: losses harvested stock by stock. Owning the index companies directly lets the manager realize losses to offset gains elsewhere; a fund cannot pass its losses through. About $55K a year after the $40K manager fee (planning estimate).
• Custom exclusions and tilts. Leave NVDA and MSFT out of the direct index and tilt away from information technology, so new money diversifies instead of adding to the concentration.
• Tax-managed transition of existing stocks. A tax-managed SMA takes NVDA, MSFT in as they are and sells them over time within the $994K yearly gain budget, instead of a one-time sale.
• Individual municipal bond ladder. Replace MUB ($9.80M) with individual bonds laddered over 1 to 10 years: known maturities and tax-exempt income, and the $600K loss in the fund can be harvested in the switch.
• Tax-aware rebalancing across accounts. Rebalancing to the CIO allocation uses losses first, stays within the gain budget, and checks wash sales across the household's accounts.

HOW THE MOVE WOULD WORK, TAX-EFFICIENTLY
• NVDA, MSFT would move as they are, without tax on the move, and be sold over time within your $994K yearly gain budget (about $0 of tax in year one after harvested losses, rather than about $2.62M if repositioned at once).
• About $1.70M of losses would be harvested in the move, worth about $405K in tax.
• $3.07M of cash would be invested in six monthly steps.

WHAT IT COSTS
• About $298K a year in the program, with no commissions, against about $55K today: +$243K a year.
• The benefits we can estimate come to about $309K a year, about $67K more than the added fee. These are illustrative estimates, not promises.

YOUR OPTIONS
• Advisory program with the CIO model, as above; with direct indexing or separate account managers where they fit.
• A lower-cost index-only option: about $244K a year, with fewer services; advisor compensation differs between options.
• Staying as you are in brokerage: you direct the portfolio, and recommendations are made in your best interest at the time they are made.

THINGS TO WEIGH
• Expected volatility rises at the CIO allocation (9.2% → 9.5%); the case is about diversification and advice, not lower volatility.
• Today's funds are already low-cost (about 2 bp), so fund savings are small.
• Trading is light (about 12% of the portfolio a year), so included trading saves only about $45K a year.

QUESTIONS YOU MAY HAVE
• Why pay an ongoing fee when I rarely trade? The fee pays for ongoing advice, portfolio construction to the CIO's allocation, monitoring and rebalancing, and tax management, not for trades. If you truly want to buy and hold with little advice, a commission account can cost less, and we will show you both.
• Do I have to sell everything to move? No. Most positions can move as they are. Appreciated holdings are sold over time within a yearly gain budget, and some may stay where they are.
• I don't want to give up my company stock. You don't have to sell it all. We can reduce it in steps that fit your tax position, protect part of it, or give some away, and we follow any trading rules that apply to you.

ENCLOSED (APPROVED MATERIALS)
• Why an advisory program: ongoing advice, one fee (Client brochure)
• What you pay, and what you get (Fee disclosure)
• Moving your portfolio without a big tax bill (One-page summary)

• COST is 58.3% of the account (58.2% direct, 0.2% through funds), above the 50% single-security limit for the advisory program.
• COST is 58.3% of the account including funds, above the 10% guideline.
• Growth leadership is narrow and expensive; earnings are broadening. Portfolios heavy in large-cap growth now sit further from the tactical target.

WHERE WE START
• The advisory program is not available at present (COST is 58.3% of the account (58.2% direct, 0.2% through funds), above the 50% single-security limit). It can be revisited once the position is below the limit.
• Staying in brokerage: about $1,650 a year in fund expenses and commissions. We start with a plan for the position.

THINGS TO WEIGH
• The benefits that can be estimated (about $7,938 a year) cover about 55% of the higher fee; ongoing advice, planning and risk management make up the rest.
• Today's funds are already low-cost (about 1 bp), so fund savings are small.
• Trading is light (about 12% of the portfolio a year), so included trading saves only about $1,485 a year.
• Not eligible for the program: COST is 58.3% of the account (58.2% direct, 0.2% through funds), above the 50% single-security limit.

QUESTIONS YOU MAY HAVE
• Why pay an ongoing fee when I rarely trade? The fee pays for ongoing advice, portfolio construction to the CIO's allocation, monitoring and rebalancing, and tax management, not for trades. If you truly want to buy and hold with little advice, a commission account can cost less, and we will show you both.
• Do I have to sell everything to move? No. Most positions can move as they are. Appreciated holdings are sold over time within a yearly gain budget, and some may stay where they are.
• My portfolio has done well. Why change it? Past returns came with more risk than your profile calls for. The proposal aims for similar expected return with less risk, and a plan if markets fall.

ENCLOSED (APPROVED MATERIALS)
• Why an advisory program: ongoing advice, one fee (Client brochure)
• What you pay, and what you get (Fee disclosure)
• Moving your portfolio without a big tax bill (One-page summary)

Figures are illustrative estimates and do not imply future results. Draft for advisor and compliance review.
